source_acquisition.search_note: The target row in reports/tables/visual_source_inventory.csv is no_public_source_found with no selected repository or files, and corpus/visual_sources/icml-2026-cd054c2b1c0a/ contains no source. The PDF metadata, body, footnotes, Impact Statement, and references expose only arXiv/DOI-style paper links, not an author code or plotting URL. Read-only gh searches for the exact title, arXiv ID 2605.03984, and author repositories found no directly matching visual source; generic index/note hits were excluded. AaronHavens/FlowMatching is an unrelated 2024 constrained flow-matching toy repository, and neta93/visual-illustrations contains a DTM-vs-FM illustration notebook/GIF; neither matches this paper’s figures, tables, or metadata. No candidate therefore meets the paper-link or repository-metadata validation requirement.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Concept figures use a related cream-to-orange-red density palette; Figure 3 uses eight categorical mode colors, Figure 4 a viridis-like sequential density map, Figure 5 black/blue/orange method overlays, and Tables 1–3 light/dark cream best/second shading. There is no cross-figure method-color contract.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: PDF text, equations, captions, table rules, table text, and table shading are vector; all five main plotting regions are raster XObjects. Figure 1 combines raster spheres with vector outer arrows/divider, while Figure 2 has masked RGB panels; Figure 3 is the lowest-resolution dense scatter, Figure 4 is high-ppi but small, and Figure 5 is a composite histogram raster.
paper_style.style_consistency: ICML double-column main layout, serif captions, Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern tables, booktabs-like rules, and cream best/second shading are consistent. Internal figure typography, raster resolution, and palettes vary substantially across conceptual diagrams, 3-D scatter, heatmaps, and histograms.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. Flow Sampling is the first diffusion sampler able to perform sampling from an unnormalized density on Riemannian manifolds. The figure depicts a learned diffusion process using iterative Flow Sampling from a mixture of spherical von Mises–Fisher distributions.

color.semantic_mapping: Pale cream is the field; orange-to-red intensity and hotspot shape encode increasing spherical density; light gray ellipses are soft shadows; the palette does not encode method identity.

encodings.x: Left-to-right stage/time direction from t=0 to t=1.
encodings.color: Orange-red density intensity across spherical snapshots.
encodings.shape: Five spherical density snapshots with soft elliptical shadows.
encodings.line: Horizontal time arrow and black divider before target q.
encodings.facet: One row of five stages: p₀, intermediate states, p₁ᵘ, and q.
encodings.text: S², p₀, p₁ᵘ, q, t=0, t, and t=1 labels.

figures.data_and_statistics: Qualitative preview for the Section 6.4 S² von Mises–Fisher mixture. The PDF gives no sample count, repetitions, concentration, K, numerical density error, or uncertainty; the five spheres are source, intermediate learned-process, learned-endpoint, and target snapshots.
figures.evidence_relation: Headline capability preview connecting the Introduction claim about Riemannian manifolds to the constant-curvature conditional drift in Section 4 and the sphere experiment in Section 6.4. It is not a baseline comparison and does not establish performance on hyperbolic or general manifolds.
design_strengths: Repeated snapshots and a horizontal arrow make source-to-target progression immediately legible.
Spherical shading and hotspots preserve geometric intuition without requiring axes.
The vertical divider separates learned p₁ᵘ from target q.
design_weaknesses: No colorbar, stage legend, numeric scale, or uncertainty display.
The p₁ᵘ/q relationship and color semantics require the surrounding text.
One qualitative S² mixture cannot quantify density error or general-manifold coverage.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use equally spaced density snapshots, an explicit time arrow, and a target divider for a complex generative process; a quantitative reuse should add a shared colorbar, stage definitions, and sample/error information.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. (left) Flow matching conditional probability path is marginal of a noising process conditioned on a data point x₁. (middle) Flow sampling conditional probability path is a marginal of a denoising process conditioned on a noise point x₀. (right) The probability of the marginal process is the same in both cases.

color.semantic_mapping: Cream background and yellow-to-orange-red filled contours encode density intensity; gray rings encode probability contours/path structure; orange points encode conditioned x₀/x₁; colors do not identify methods.

encodings.x: Conceptual spatial direction from source toward target.
encodings.color: Filled density intensity in each toy probability path.
encodings.shape: Orange conditioned points x₀ and x₁.
encodings.line: Gray contour rings and path overlays.
encodings.facet: Flow Matching conditional / Flow Sampling conditional (ours) / Marginal.
encodings.text: Panel titles and p₀, q, x₀, x₁ labels.

figures.data_and_statistics: Qualitative 2-D toy density illustration. There are no units, samples, replications, aggregation, numeric axes, or uncertainty; spatial positions and contour levels are explanatory rather than quantities to read off.
figures.evidence_relation: Method-interface figure immediately following Equations (13)–(16), externalizing Proposition 3.1 and the conditioning reversal: target-conditioned FM versus source-conditioned denoising with a shared marginal. It is theory/mechanism evidence, not an empirical result or ablation.
design_strengths: Three aligned panels use the same dimensions and background for direct construction-to-construction comparison.
Direct labels avoid a legend and keep conditioning points visible.
The right panel visually overlays the two constructions to support the same-marginal claim.
design_weaknesses: No coordinate range or color scale permits numeric density comparison.
Dense overlapping contours in the right panel require caption and body text to decode.
Rasterized panels prevent precise reading and do not show uncertainty.
figures.reusable_pattern: Align a conditional process, its reversed-conditioning counterpart, and their common marginal in fixed-size direct-labelled panels; preserve shared scales and define points, contours, and color semantics in the caption.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3. Ala4 molecular structures represented by torsion coordinates (ϕ₁, ϕ₂, ϕ₃) with 2³ distinct modes.

family: Nimbus Roman No9 L panel labels

color.semantic_mapping: Eight categorical colors represent the 2³ Ala4 torsion modes and are reused across ASBS, Flow Sampling, and MD panels.

encodings.x: ϕ₁ torsion angle with ticks −π, 0, π.
encodings.y: ϕ₂ torsion angle with ticks −π, 0, π; ϕ₃ is the third 3-D axis.
encodings.shape: Point marks in a 3-D scatter cloud.
encodings.line: 3-D box axes and light gray grid only.
encodings.text: ϕ₁, ϕ₂, ϕ₃, −π/0/π ticks, and panel labels.

figures.data_and_statistics: The body reports eight Ala4 metastable modes. Appendix B says the 5×10⁷ MD test samples were subsampled to 50,000 for this 3-D scatter; the figure reports no replication, density scale, error, denominator, or numeric coverage statistic.
figures.evidence_relation: Qualitative mode-coverage comparison between ASBS, Flow Sampling, and MD reference in Section 6.2. It complements Table 2’s quantitative Ala2 metrics and supports the body’s statement that Flow Sampling covers all eight modes, but it is not a distribution-distance result, proof, or component ablation.
design_strengths: A common camera, coordinate limits, and panel arrangement enable direct method/reference comparison.
Reused categorical colors make mode locations traceable across panels in a color display.
design_weaknesses: No legend maps the eight colors to named modes.
Dense 3-D overplotting and occlusion make concentration hard to judge.
Small single-object raster panels and low native 239–247 ppi lose point detail; no quantitative uncertainty or coverage scale is shown.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a same-camera 3-D triptych with fixed coordinate bounds and mode colors to compare generator and reference; add a mode legend, transparency/density cue, and explicit coverage statistic for formal reporting.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4. Ala2 Ramachandran plots over 10⁶ samples.

family: Nimbus Roman No9 L panel labels

color.semantic_mapping: Viridis-like purple-to-yellow intensity encodes normalized 2-D torsion density; white bins encode no observed count rather than a method or error state.

encodings.x: ϕ torsion angle over approximately [−π, π] with −3…3 ticks.
encodings.y: ψ torsion angle over approximately [−π, π] with −3…3 ticks.
encodings.text: ϕ, ψ, −3…3 ticks, and panel labels.

figures.data_and_statistics: The caption reports 10⁶ samples. Appendix C.1 defines mdtraj-derived angles binned into a 200×200 histogram on [−π,π]×[−π,π] and normalized into a discrete distribution; the figure has no replication or uncertainty display, and white bins indicate zero observed count.
figures.evidence_relation: Qualitative joint-density check for the Ala2 D_KL/JSD/energy-W₂ results in Table 2. It compares ASBS, Flow Sampling, and MD spatial structure and is an empirical diagnostic, not an ablation or proof.
design_strengths: Same coordinate bounds across all three panels expose mode locations and empty regions directly.
A continuous density field complements Table 2’s scalar divergence metrics.
design_weaknesses: No colorbar, normalization note, panel-specific range, or explicit empty-bin key.
White empty bins can be confused with missing image area.
The left-column display is small, while the short caption omits methods, units, and bin settings.
figures.reusable_pattern: Bind a same-scale heatmap triptych to a divergence table as a joint-distribution cross-check; add a shared colorbar, fixed normalization, angular units, and an empty-bin definition.

figures.label: Figure 5
figures.module: Appendix B.1 Interatomic Distance and Energy Histograms

caption.text: Figure 5. Ala2 interatomic distance and energy histogram over 10⁴ samples evaluated against the MD data as reference.

color.semantic_mapping: Black is MD Reference, blue is Flow Sampling, and orange is ASBS; all three use step-outline histograms.

encodings.x: Interatomic distance in the left panel; energy in the right panel.
encodings.color: Reference / Flow Sampling / ASBS method overlays.
encodings.text: Axis labels and a repeated three-item legend in each panel.

figures.data_and_statistics: The caption reports 10⁴ samples; Appendix B.1 compares two empirical distributions against MD reference data. The PDF does not state bin width, physical units, replicate count, uncertainty, or denominator, so peaks and tails are descriptive diagnostics.
figures.evidence_relation: Appendix qualitative diagnostic for the Ala2 divergence and energy-W₂ metrics in Table 2; the body points to Section B for these energy-histogram plots. It adds distribution-shape evidence but no new metric, proof, or ablation.
design_strengths: The same reference and two methods are overlaid, preserving peak and tail shape.
Paired distance and energy views cover complementary aspects of conformer fidelity.
design_weaknesses: Bin width, physical units, normalization, and uncertainty are absent.
Repeated legends consume space and can cover low-density tails.
Rasterization and unconstrained x ranges make small tail differences difficult to interpret.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use paired histogram overlays to check geometric distance and energy distributions; add units, bin rules, reference-sample definition, and a shared legend, with replicate variation when the comparison is inferential.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1. Results for the synthetic energy function experiments. We report a geometric 𝒲₂ metric Klein et al. (2024) and 1D energy histogram E(·) 𝒲₂ metric with respect to ground truth samples. See Section A.4 for more details. We use light and dark shading to denote best and 2nd best result respectively. † We include baseline measurements over random subsets of the ground truth samples. This can be considered the “optimal” value for that metric, which was not clear in previous instantiations of this benchmark. Flow Sampling XL results are omitted for DW4 due to minimal improvement. Mean and standard error are reported across 5 training runs.

tables.uncertainty: Mean ± standard error across five training runs for learned methods; the ground-truth subset row has random-subset variation rather than training-run variation.
tables.data_and_statistics: Three synthetic targets (DW-4, LJ-13, LJ-55) crossed with geometric W₂ and 1-D energy-histogram E(·)W₂, both lower-is-better. PIS, DDS, iDEM, AS, ASBS, Flow Sampling, Flow Sampling XL, and Subsets of MCMC ground-truth reference are compared; selected entries use scientific notation.
tables.evidence_relation: Headline synthetic-accuracy comparison connecting the state-of-the-art claim and Section 6.1 baseline list to the metric definitions in Appendix A.4 and the conclusion’s Table 1 reference. It is a main result, not a component ablation.
design_strengths: Dataset-by-metric grouping and downward arrows make the decision direction explicit.
Caption defines best/second shading, uncertainty, the MCMC reference row, and the XL omission.
design_weaknesses: Dense method rows and E(·)W₂ notation require the appendix for full interpretation.
No runtime, energy-call, or wall-clock column supports an efficiency claim.
Ground-truth subset variation is statistically different from learned-method training repeats, and LJ-55 error scales are heterogeneous.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a dataset×metric grouped benchmark matrix with direction arrows, a reference row, best/second shading, and explicit uncertainty; add an adjacent cost definition when efficiency is part of the claim.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2. Results for ALA2. We report D_KL on 1-D marginals for ϕ and ψ, Jensen–Shannon divergence (JSD) on the joint distribution of torsion angles (ϕ, ψ), and an energy-histogram 𝒲₂ metric with respect to ground-truth samples. Light and dark shading denote the best and second-best method respectively.

tables.uncertainty: Cells display ± values, but the PDF caption does not define whether they are test-molecule spread, run variability, standard deviation, or standard error; no repetition count is supplied.
tables.data_and_statistics: Ala2 D_KL on 1-D ϕ/ψ marginals, joint torsion-angle JSD, and energy-histogram W₂, all lower-is-better, across NFE(Train)=1024, 256, 128, and 64 for ASBS and Flow Sampling. Very large low-budget energy-W₂ values use scientific notation.
tables.evidence_relation: Main comparison and low-NFE robustness/efficiency sensitivity. It pairs with Figure 4’s joint density, Figure 5’s appendix histogram, and the Section 6.5 NFE discussion; the sweep is not a component-deletion ablation or proof.
design_strengths: The multi-level header separates 1-D marginal from joint metrics.
Explicit NFE rows expose the budget–quality relationship, with arrows, grouping, and shading aiding scanability.
design_weaknesses: Single-column width makes small type and ± values tight.
Uncertainty semantics, sample counts, run counts, and physical units are absent.
No wall-clock or energy-call cost column accompanies the NFE proxy.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a method×budget sweep with metric-family headers and retain low-budget failures in the table; define the statistical unit of ± and the relationship between NFE and actual cost.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3. Results on large-scale amortized conformer generation, evaluated on two test sets, SPICE and GEOM-DRUGS using the same 12-layer EGNN architecture across all methods. We report the coverage recall and precision (%) and Absolute Mean RMSD (AMR) for the threshold 1.25Å and standard deviation across test molecules. See Section 6.3 and Appendix C for details. Precision coverage was not reported in ASBS (Liu et al., 2025a). † Re-implementation with logit normal time weighting. * Auxiliary network roughly doubles the number of network evaluation during optimization.

tables.uncertainty: Caption defines ± as standard deviation across test molecules; missing ASBS precision and some low-NFE AS ± cells are shown with dashes rather than imputed values.
tables.data_and_statistics: SPICE and GEOM-DRUGS are crossed with coverage recall/precision (%) and AMR at a 1.25 Å RMSD threshold. Rows cover RDKit ETKDG, ASBS* at NFE 512, AS† at 256/128/64, and Flow Sampling at 256/128/64; the caption reports the shared 12-layer EGNN and test-molecule SD.
tables.evidence_relation: Headline amortized-conformer and efficiency-cost comparison supporting the 4–8× training-cost discussion. It connects the NFE sweep to Section 6.3 cost reasoning and Appendix C.2 configuration; it is not an ablation or formal runtime measurement.
design_strengths: Dataset×recall/precision×coverage/AMR hierarchy preserves metric semantics and direction arrows.
Shared architecture and NFE budgets make the comparison’s intended fairness visible.
Missing values use short dashes instead of fabricated zeros.
design_weaknesses: Ten columns remain dense even across both columns.
Unreported ASBS precision leaves the horizontal precision comparison incomplete.
Unequal NFE budgets and test-molecule SD do not isolate training-repeat uncertainty; no actual time or energy column turns NFE into wall-clock cost.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a dataset×metric hierarchy that combines quality, budget, and missing-state notation; define how NFE, network evaluations, and actual cost relate before making efficiency claims.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4. Hyperparameters for the synthetic energy experiments. We report the architecture, replay-buffer configuration, and optimization settings used for DW-4, LJ-13, and LJ-55.

tables.uncertainty: None; this is a fixed configuration matrix rather than a result table.
tables.data_and_statistics: Eleven valued hyperparameter rows grouped as Model, Base SDE, Replay buffer, and Training across Hyperparameter, DW-4, LJ-13, and LJ-55 columns. Values mix integers, thousands separators, scientific notation, and decimal-formatted constants; adaptive γ points to Appendix A Equation (49).
tables.evidence_relation: Reproduction/experimental-design interface for Table 1’s synthetic architecture, SDE, replay-buffer, and optimization settings. It supplies configuration details, not a theorem, experiment result, or ablation.
design_strengths: Semantic row groups map directly to model and training stages.
Three target columns make shared versus task-specific settings easy to inspect.
Fixed settings are not presented as uncertainty or performance evidence.
design_weaknesses: Seeds, hardware, optimizer details, and stopping criteria are not in the matrix.
Learning-rate scientific notation and other numeric formats are inconsistent.
The adaptive γ meaning requires a separate equation lookup.
tables.reusable_pattern: Organize reproduction parameters into Model/Base SDE/Replay buffer/Training groups and align task variants as columns; state the experiment family in the caption.

tables.label: Table 5
tables.module: Appendix B/C.2 Hyperparameters and Architecture Details

caption.text: Table 5. Hyperparameters for the alanine peptide experiments. Model and training hyperparameters used for alanine dipeptide (Ala2) and alanine tetrapeptide (Ala4).

tables.uncertainty: None; this is a fixed Ala2/Ala4 configuration matrix rather than a result table.
tables.data_and_statistics: Fifteen valued rows grouped as Model, Base SDE, Replay buffer, and Training across Hyperparameter, Ala2, and Ala4 columns. The matrix includes radial-cutoff Å units, shared architecture/source/buffer settings, task-specific learning rates and clipping, and adaptive γ via Equation (49).
tables.evidence_relation: Reproduction interface for Table 2, Figures 3–5, and the large-scale conformer configuration; Appendix C.2 adds the 12-layer EGNN, buffer, GPU, and low-NFE context. It does not constitute an ablation or proof.
design_strengths: Ala2 and Ala4 variants are aligned as parallel columns.
Row groups match Table 4, making shared model/SDE/buffer/training semantics portable.
design_weaknesses: The narrow table leaves parameter semantics and units partly to adjacent prose and equations.
Seeds, hardware, stopping criteria, and actual energy-call records are not tabulated.
Harmonic-source σ and noise-scaling γ schedule/units require formula lookup.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use one shared hyperparameter matrix for model-family task variants, retaining semantic row groups and units; place budget and environment details in adjacent columns or text.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 gives the S²/Riemannian capability headline; Figure 2 explains source-conditioned denoising versus flow-matching conditioning; Table 1 supplies the synthetic benchmark comparison; Figure 3, Figure 4, and Table 2 pair peptide mode/joint-density views with an NFE sweep; Table 3 extends the claim to large-scale conformer generation and low-NFE efficiency; Figure 5 adds an appendix distance/energy diagnostic.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Every object uses an italic Figure/Table label followed by Roman prose. Table captions are more self-contained, defining metrics, directions, shading, missingness, and uncertainty; Figure 2 is the most complete figure caption, while Figures 3–5 defer method, scale, units, and color semantics to the body or appendix.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Main result tables use hierarchical dataset/metric headers with ↑/↓ direction markers; Table 3 expands this to dataset×recall/precision×coverage/AMR. Appendix tables use Hyperparameter×task columns and italic row groups for Model, Base SDE, Replay buffer, and Training.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2 directly externalizes Equations (13)–(16) and the conditioning mechanism. Table 1 binds synthetic baselines to Appendix A metrics; Table 2 is an NFE robustness/efficiency sensitivity; Table 3 binds amortized results to NFE cost discussion. There is no independent component-deletion ablation object; Tables 4–5 are reproduction matrices.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Table 1 points to Appendix A.4, Table 2 and Figure 4 to Appendix B/C definitions, Table 3 to Appendix C, and the body points to Section B for Figure 5. Tables 4–5 supply synthetic and peptide settings; Appendices D–E contain target-law comparisons and proofs without additional figures or tables.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Serif body/caption typography and embedded Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern table text remain stable across main and appendix objects. Figure interiors switch among raster serif/math, DejaVu Sans/mathtext, and small panel labels, so cross-object readability depends on rendering rather than a single plotting style.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Light/dark cream best/second shading is the clearest cross-object convention across Tables 1–3. Figures 1–2 share a related density palette, but Figure 3 mode colors, Figure 4 viridis, and Figure 5 method colors are independent and cannot track a method across plots.

most_reusable_patterns: Dataset×metric multi-level headers with direction arrows, best/second shading, and caption-defined uncertainty for a main comparison (Table 1).
Method×NFE sweeps paired with matched distribution triptychs/overlays to connect budget robustness with distribution shape (Table 2, Figures 4–5).
Semantic appendix hyperparameter matrices organized as Model/Base SDE/Replay buffer/Training (Tables 4–5).
Direct-labelled three-panel concept diagrams or repeated density snapshots for source/target conditioning and manifold processes (Figures 1–2).
highest_value_objects: Table 1 — highest information density for the synthetic headline comparison.
Table 3 — most direct object for the large-scale amortized and efficiency claim.
Figure 2 — clearest interface to the conditioning mechanism.
Figure 4 — most direct joint-density cross-check for Table 2.
failure_patterns: No publicly validated plotting/table/LaTeX source; figure typography, HEX values, and line widths are rendered estimates.
Figures 1–4 omit shared scales, legends, or complete method/unit definitions; Figure 3 lacks an eight-mode legend and Figure 4 lacks a colorbar.
Table 2 leaves ± semantics undefined, while Table 3’s test-molecule SD does not replace training-repeat uncertainty; ASBS precision and some low-NFE cells are missing.
NFE is used as a training-cost proxy without wall-clock, energy-call, or network-evaluation columns, so the 4–8× claim cannot be visually audited as actual time.
Raster figure typography, resolution, and color contracts vary; Figure 3’s dense scatter is especially degraded by low native resolution and small display scale.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses double-column capability/mechanism diagrams, benchmark tables, and compact distribution comparisons to trace method interface → synthetic performance → low-NFE peptide evidence → large-scale efficiency, then uses appendix histograms and hyperparameter tables for diagnostics and reproduction.
